honest_gaps: 5 of the 7 fusion strategies are aliases today (claim C8). Differentiating them is real unstarted work: conditional-hybrid needs `when` guards on grafted stages, ensemble needs the donated stages in PARALLEL under a quorum barrier, progressive needs escalation gates.
The forge fuses exactly TWO sources. N-way fusion (spec :10849 'ensemble') is not implemented; chaining pairwise would work but is untested and the lineage record assumes one donor prefix (d1.).

The four axes are STRUCTURAL predicates over the document, not runtime outcomes. The spec says 'on representative cases' and this measures what the document guarantees, not what an execution produced. A workflow that declares every mitigation and then fails in practice would score identically. Settling experiment: execute both sources and the fusion on a real task and compare receipts - that requires the runtime, which is not this unit.
IMPROVEMENT_EPSILON=0.01 and REGRESSION_TOLERANCE=0.0 are chosen, not derived. A different epsilon changes the CERTIFIED/REJECTED split; measured sensitivity was not swept.

Scout ranks 163 registry rows on DECLARED (prose) capabilities and can never structurally verify them - by construction those rows have no DSL document. Every hit is tagged with its derivation and a DECLARED profile reports zero hazard coverage, so a prose row can never win a hazard-demanding goal.

The pair search covered 26 of 97 blueprints (325 pairs). The full 97x96/2 = 4,656 pairs were not swept; the reported CERTIFIED/REJECTED ratio is for that 26-candidate slice, alphabetically first by id, NOT for the whole corpus.

27 registry candidates have a provenance anchor that does not resolve. This unit REPORTS them and excludes them from ADOPT recommendations; it did not repair them (they belong to the archaeology lanes).
